summary.text: A 41-year-old married man was admitted on March 5, 2026 with 1 day of right lower limb redness, swelling and exudation, with an unremarkable past medical history. On admission he was intubated and ventilated, with blood pressure 82/46 mmHg with atrial flutter at 150 beats/min and temperature 38.9 °C, with extensive erythema, blistering and copious exudate from the right ankle to the groin.

Initial testing showed Pro-BNP 12,140.5 pg/mL, elevated high-sensitivity troponin T, CRP 214.0 mg/L, lactate 4.6 mmol/L, and transthoracic echocardiography with four-chamber enlargement, LVEF 16% and a 29 × 25 mm left ventricular apical thrombus. Wound culture confirmed Aeromonas hydrophila. He was diagnosed with necrotizing fasciitis, septic shock, MODS and severe dilated cardiomyopathy with heart failure.

Management began with urgent surgical debridement and piperacillin-tazobactam plus clindamycin, later escalated to imipenem-cilastatin plus levofloxacin, with norepinephrine, dobutamine, amiodarone and esmolol, anticoagulation and CRRT. On March 8 he returned for further debridement under TEE guidance with cardiac-sparing induction, volume restriction and a 20° head-up tilt; lactate fell to 1.7 mmol/L and hemodynamics stayed stable.

Postoperatively he went to the ICU intubated on norepinephrine and dobutamine; TEE showed LVEF 20% with no thrombus displacement. Local infection and CRP improved, vasoactive agents were weaned, and TTE on Day 5 showed LVEF 22%. He left the ICU on postoperative day 10 and the hospital on day 21; at 1 month LVEF was 28% with a smaller 18 × 15 mm thrombus, on warfarin and guideline-directed heart failure therapy, and he was alive at last follow-up.
